bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged patch.diff / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ in `exif_get_sshort` on the exact staged 512-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_37226/poc`. The outer EXIF parser reaches a MakerNote entry, reads its original-buffer offset field as `doff = 26`, copies 96 bytes from that offset, and the copied blob begins `Apple iOS\0\0\0II*\0`, so `interpret_maker_note()` selects the Apple MakerNote loader and stores `md->offset = 26`. In `exif_mnote_data_apple_load()`, the loader computes `ofs = d->offset + 6 = 32`, reads nested byte order `II`, and then interprets bytes `2a 00` at `buf + ofs + 14` as `tcount = 42`. The vulnerable pre-loop check `buf_size < 6 + 16 + tcount * 6 + 4` therefore asks only for 278 bytes and ignores both the 26-byte MakerNote offset and the actual 12-byte Apple entry width; the 512-byte witness passes even though 42 entries would require 556 bytes. After `ofs += 16`, the loop advances 12 bytes per claimed entry through the original input buffer. On iteration `i = 39`, `ofs` becomes `516`, and `d->entries[i].tag = exif_get_short(buf + ofs, d->order)` calls `exif_get_sshort()` on `buf + 516`, where the Intel branch reads `buf[1]` at address 517. AddressSanitizer reports that 1-byte read 5 bytes past the 512-byte heap region. The staged fix corrects the pre-loop size formula to `d->offset + 6 + 16 + tcount * 12 + 4` and adds an `ofs + 12 > buf_size` guard inside the entry loop.

source.description: First project-side read of the MakerNote entry's value offset. This creates the attacker-controlled original-buffer offset later saved as `offset_mnote` and reused as the Apple MakerNote parser base.
source.value_from: In the staged EXIF-IFD MakerNote entry, the 4-byte value-offset field is `1a 00 00 00`. This statement decodes it as `doff = 26`, the exact original-buffer offset later passed into the Apple loader.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The Intel branch dereferences the second byte of the 16-bit word requested by `exif_mnote_data_apple_load`; on the witnessed `i = 39` iteration that pointer is `original_input + 516`, so `buf[1]` reads address 517, five bytes past the 512-byte heap region.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `libexif/exif-utils.c:94:40` with stack `exif_get_sshort -> exif_get_short -> exif_mnote_data_apple_load`, and the faulting address is 5 bytes to the right of the 512-byte input region.

root_cause.description: Incorrect pre-loop bounds check. The vulnerable formula underestimates the bytes needed for the claimed Apple entry table by using `tcount * 6` instead of 12-byte entries and by omitting the attacker-controlled MakerNote base offset.
root_cause.note: With `tcount = 42`, this condition asks only for 278 bytes, so the 512-byte witness is accepted even though reaching all 42 entries from `d->offset = 26` would require 556 bytes. The staged patch fixes the formula to `d->offset + 6 + 16 + tcount * 12 + 4` and also adds `if (ofs + 12 > buf_size)` inside the loop.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-driving attacker-controlled count is created here. Because the parser starts at `d->offset + 6 = 32`, this read reinterprets the nested TIFF fixed-value bytes `2a 00` as `tcount = 42`, which then drives both the broken size check and the entry loop bound.

parser_admitted.description: The copied MakerNote blob matches the Apple signature, so `interpret_maker_note()` allocates the Apple-specific decoder and later calls its vulnerable `load` method on the full 512-byte witness.
parser_admitted.note: Step 2 copies bytes beginning `Apple iOS\0`, so `exif_mnote_data_apple_identify()` returns nonzero on this path.

coarse_trace.summary: The outer EXIF parser reads the MakerNote entry's value offset, copies the 96-byte payload starting at original-buffer offset 26, and preserves that offset as `offset_mnote`.
MakerNote dispatch recognizes the copied payload as Apple, creates an Apple MakerNote decoder, and stores `md->offset = 26` before loading from the full witness buffer.

The Apple loader computes `ofs = 32`, chooses Intel byte order, misreads nested bytes `2a 00` as `tcount = 42`, and the pre-loop size check underestimates the bytes required for 42 claimed 12-byte entries.
The 42-entry loop advances its cursor to `ofs = 516` on entry 39, and the Intel 16-bit reader performs the saved out-of-bounds read five bytes past the 512-byte heap input.

fine_trace.note: While loading the MakerNote entry, this reads its 4-byte value-offset field `1a 00 00 00` and materializes `doff = 26`. That original-buffer offset is the base later reused by the Apple MakerNote parser.

Copies the 96-byte MakerNote payload from `d + 26` into the entry object. The copied bytes begin `Apple iOS\0\0\0II*\0`, which both identify the Apple variant and carry the nested fields the Apple loader misparses.

Because this entry is the MakerNote tag, the parser preserves the same original-buffer offset in `offset_mnote`. `interpret_maker_note()` later passes that field into the Apple decoder as its base offset.
The copied payload starts with `Apple iOS\0`, so the Apple-specific MakerNote variant is selected instead of abandoning maker-note parsing.
The Apple decoder stores `md->offset = 26`. The later load routine adds 6 to this attacker-controlled base to locate the nested Apple structure inside the original buffer.
Derives the start of the Apple-specific nested data inside the original input buffer. With `d->offset = 26`, this sets `ofs = 32`.
Bytes `buf[ofs + 12]` and `buf[ofs + 13]` are `I` and `I`, so the loader chooses Intel byte order for every later 16-bit and 32-bit field read in this MakerNote blob.
Reads bytes `2a 00` at file offsets 46-47 and interprets them as `tcount = 42`. Those bytes are actually the nested TIFF fixed value, but the vulnerable Apple loader reuses them as its entry count.

Root cause. With `tcount = 42`, this underestimates the required size as 278 bytes. It omits the 26-byte MakerNote base offset and treats each claimed entry as 6 bytes even though the loop consumes 12 bytes, so the 512-byte witness incorrectly passes a check that should require 556 bytes.
Advances the cursor from 32 to 48, which the loop treats as the start of the first 12-byte Apple entry record in the original buffer.

The loop trusts `tcount = 42` and advances 12 bytes per claimed entry from the cursor in step 10. By iteration `i = 39`, the current entry start is `48 + 39 * 12 = 516`, already 4 bytes past the 512-byte buffer, but the vulnerable source has no `ofs + 12 > buf_size` stop before reading that entry.
On the `i = 39` iteration from step 11, this call passes `buf + 516` to the 16-bit reader even though the valid input region ends at byte 511.

Sink. In the Intel branch, `exif_get_sshort` dereferences `buf[1]` from the pointer supplied in step 12. With `buf == original_input + 516`, that second byte is address 517, matching ASan's report of a 1-byte read 5 bytes past the 512-byte heap region.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 5 bytes to the right of the 512-byte heap buffer the libFuzzer driver allocated for the staged witness.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the same vulnerable function: it replaces the under-bounded pre-loop formula with `d->offset + 6 + 16 + tcount * 12 + 4` and adds an `ofs + 12 > buf_size` stop at the loop head, which would reject or stop the witnessed path before `buf + 516` is read.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_37226 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `exif_from_data_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `exif_get_sshort` with stack `exif_get_short -> exif_mnote_data_apple_load`.

format.name: EXIF data with Apple MakerNote
format.contract: The input must be EXIF data whose MakerNote entry resolves to original-buffer offset `26`, whose copied MakerNote payload begins `Apple iOS\0`, and whose Apple substructure makes `exif_mnote_data_apple_load()` compute `ofs = 32`, choose Intel byte order, and read `tcount = 42` from bytes 46-47 of the 512-byte buffer; under the vulnerable code, that count passes the under-bounded pre-loop check and drives the entry loop to `buf + 516`.
